content.text: If you purchase a product or register for an account through one of the links on our site, we may receive compensation. Learn more > With Michigan back in the Final Four, the "Fab Five" is reuniting for the Wolverines' national semifinal game Saturday.Juwan Howard, Ray Jackson, Jimmy King, Jalen Rose and Chris Webber helped transform college basketball more than three decades ago, presaging an era where it's the norm rather than the exception for freshmen to dominate the sport in a given season. In 1992, they comprised the first all-freshman starting lineup in an NCAA championship game as the Wolverines fell to Duke, and they reached the final the next year as sophomores but lost to North Carolina. Their legacy took a hit in a subsequent scandal centered around Webber receiving money from a longtime booster, but remain a touchstone to the glory years of Michigan basketball. The five don't often appear in public together, but they will reunite for Saturday's game between Michigan and Arizona alongside host Adam Lefkoe. Here's everything you need to know about where and when to watch the Fab Five, together again at the Final Four.Where to watch 'Fab Five' altcast of Michigan-ArizonaTV channel: truTVLive stream: DIRECTVThe "Fab Five" alternate broadcast of Michigan vs. Arizona will air on truTV and can be streamed live via DIRECTV, which offers a free trial to new users. Michigan vs. Arizona Final Four game timeDate: Saturday, April 4Time: Approximately 8:49 p.m. ETThe Michigan vs. Arizona game is tentatively slated to begin Saturday at 8:49 p.m. ET, but the actual tip will come 25 to 30 minutes after the conclusion of the UConn vs. Illinois semifinal. The games will be played at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Who are the Fab Five? The Fab Five are Michigan's Class of 1991 recruits who reached the NCAA championship game as freshmen and sophomores. They are: Chris WebberJalen RoseJuwan HowardJimmy KingRay JacksonWebber was the star recruit of the bunch, a Detroit native who was named national player of the year as a high school senior, but Rose was the floor leader when the group gathered in Ann Arbor. Howard was the steady man in the middle and went on to win an NBA championship with the Miami Heat. King and Jackson were Texas natives and only Jackson from the group did not play in the NBA after college.
